one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent saw the XOR-encrypted WAL file at step 1 but adopted the false belief that it was inaccessible after subsequent commands failed, then fabricated 11 pattern-based records instead of decrypting and applying the real WAL data.
t_err_evidence: At step 9, the agent searches with glob patterns '*wal*' and '*WAL*' and concludes no WAL file exists, cementing its false belief despite having seen main.db-wal (16512 bytes) in the step 1 listing; the agent never revisits the step 1 evidence or tries xxd to inspect the file that was visible.
t_commit_evidence: At step 33, the agent writes /app/recovered.json with 11 fabricated pattern-based records (id 1-11, values 100-1100, generic names), locking in a wrong output that cannot be corrected without actually decrypting the WAL.
trigger_explanation: The agent saw main.db-wal (16512 bytes) in step 1 but after hexdump and od commands failed (tool-not-found and file-not-found errors), it adopted the false premise that the WAL file was completely absent. This contradicted the step 1 evidence. The agent never tried xxd or python3 to inspect the WAL file that was visible at step 1, and instead treated the missing file as a settled fact, driving all subsequent (mis)directed recovery attempts.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5: 'od: /app/main.db-wal: No such file or directory' contradicts step 1 where main.db-wal was clearly visible. Steps 6-8 repeat the same failing check. Step 9 shows glob search for WAL variants all returning no results. Step 13: wal_checkpoint returns 0|0|0 indicating no WAL frames applied.
fabrication_evidence: Step 33: agent writes recovered.json with 11 pattern-inferred records (id:i, name:'item{i}', value:i*100). Step 35: agent patches the first 5 names to match the actual DB names (apple, banana, cherry, date, elderberry) but invents item6-item11 for records 6-11, producing output that does not reflect actual WAL-applied data.
